newsitem.title: USA: U.S Spot Products - Chicago gasoline catches fire.
newsitem.headline: U.S Spot Products - Chicago gasoline catches fire.

text.p: Gasoline markets in Chicago provided the best fireworks in otherwise subdued trade in spot refined oil products early Friday east of the Rocky Mountains as refiners bought early June barrels, traders said.
Activity in Houston was quiet following a week of yo-yo action on the highly volatile "M1" regular unleaded conventional grade, while in New York action was hurt by the transition to the June market.
The underlying NYMEX markets seemed to be garnering much of traders' attention ahead of the expiry of June products.

Still, action in that realm was subdued as well, with nearby June gasoline selling off sharply and July unleaded only half as weak. Nearby June heat, on the other hand, firmed a touch while the July contract sold off moderately.
MIDCONTINENT

A sharp move in Chicago gasoline markets that saw differentials on prompt early-June material blow out a cent in the last 24 hours to 3.50 cents over July NYMEX had some players wondering whether some refiners were having processing problems.
"This kind of move is typically associated with some kind of refiner problem," said one trader in the region.

But just as on the U.S. Gulf Coast earlier in the week when refiner buying stoked diffs on M1, no one could reliably say where the processing problems were coming from, nor could anyone point to extraordinarily liquid markets for feedstocks like naphtha or vacuum gas oil that might suggest someone's plant was really coughing.

Elswhere in the midcontinent, activity looked to be subdued, particularly in Group Three, where talk on May barrels seemed history and talk on June barrels hadn't yet heated up in earnest, traders said.
NEW YORK HARBOR

Similar transitional factors sapped liquidity in New York Harbor, though a firming trend in premium gasolines on the back of firmness in Houston earlier in the week kept trade from becoming too soporific ahead of the weekend.
Traders said prompt "D2" 93-octane premium reformulated got done on Friday at 9.00 cents over June versus an offering price of 8.25 cents over Thursday.
Heating oil in the New York Harbor eased Friday as sellers made a last bid to sell June barrels when buyers preffered July barrels that were slightly cheaper against the NYMEX contract.
The June NYMEX refined products contract was expiring Friday, putting deals on hold until the July contract becomes the benchmark.

Number two oil was offered at 0.20 cent under the June contract versus 0.10 cent under late Thursday. Low sulfur diesel was offered at 0.50 cent over, slightly firmer than the offer of 0.65 cent under Thursday.
"It's a really illiquid market. On expiry day, it's always really quiet. Dealers are waiting for July (supply)," said a Harbor dealer.

Indeed, the jet fuel market has been so thin that dealers said two sellers earlier in the week were able to push low sulphur jet to an offer of 2.25 over the June contract where it has stayed since Thursday versus 1.75 cents Wednesday.

Supply of conventional prompt unleaded gasoline was seen a touch tighter than it has been in recent days, though values were steady with the bid/ask spread at 2.50 cents and three cents under the NYMEX June contract.
U.S. GULF COAST
U.S. Gulf Coast markets were quiet Friday ahead of the June 2nd scheduling deadling for the back 16th Colonial Pipeline. Traders said they do not expect activity to pick up until Monday.
"Things are very quiet today. Most people are playing the Merc," said a Houston-based products trader.
In the U.S. Gulf, spot unleaded differentials remained steady at 1.50/1.25 cents under NYMEX June gasoline. Prompt two oil also held at 2.60/2.35 under NYMEX June heating oil.
-- New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
